title: h57yx0
The Imams after Karbala: from Imam Zayn al-Abidin to Imam al-Mahdi
hook: How did a young imam who came out of Karbala alive begin a chain of guidance that moved forward through knowledge and patience?
scenes.0.text: **Imam Husayn** was martyred at Karbala. The imamate passed to his sick son, **Imam Zayn al-Abidin**. His name was Ali. He had not been able to fight on the field. He had survived in the tent. He returned to Medina by way of captivity. Leadership did not end with the sword. It continued through a sick young man.
scenes.1.text: **Imam al-Sajjad** lived in Medina in worship and prayer. His prayers were collected in the Sahifa al-Sajjadiyya. The Ahl al-Bayt call this book "the Psalms of the Family of Muhammad." The Risalat al-Huquq is also attributed to him. Around 94 AH he was buried in al-Baqi', beside his uncle **Imam Hasan**. According to the report, he was poisoned. This orphan of Karbala left his prayer as an inheritance to the community.
scenes.1.art.actors.0.label: ms2fd7
Imam Zayn al-Abidin
scenes.2.text: His son is known as **Imam Muhammad al-Baqir**. This name means the one who splits knowledge open and reaches its depths. He founded a study circle in Medina. His son **Imam Ja'far**, along with Qatada, al-Zuhri and al-Awza'i, was also beside him. Around 114 AH he was buried in al-Baqi'. The knowledge that came from Ghadir continued in this circle.
scenes.2.art.actors.0.label: uwc4s1
Imam Muhammad al-Baqir
scenes.3.text: **Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq** turned to knowledge without becoming involved in the revolts. Ja'fari jurisprudence bears his name. He died in Medina in 148 AH. Here leadership was a circle of knowledge without a sword. This knowledge kept the community on course from the right ablution to the right imam.
scenes.3.art.actors.0.label: 1ytn1vq
Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq
scenes.4.text: Abu Hanifa and Malik are mentioned among those who benefited from the circle of **Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq**. The saying "Had it not been for those two years, Nu'man would have perished" is attributed to Abu Hanifa. It is also reported that Malik heard hadith from him. This circle of knowledge remained open in Medina.
scenes.4.art.actors.0.label: 1e0ppdj
Abu Hanifa
scenes.4.art.actors.1.label: 1ytn1vq
Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq
scenes.4.art.actors.2.label: 144jybx
Malik b. Anas
scenes.5.text: **Imam Musa al-Kazim** was known in Medina for his knowledge and patience. Harun al-Rashid had him taken to Baghdad. He spent his last four years in prison and under surveillance. He died in Baghdad in 183 AH. His tomb is in al-Kazimayn. It is reported that his death was by the order of a Barmakid. Leadership did not end in the dungeon either.
scenes.5.art.actors.0.label: 174g0gs
Imam Musa al-Kazim
scenes.5.art.actors.1.label: fgbs84
Harun al-Rashid
scenes.6.text: Ma'mun summoned **Imam Ali al-Rida** to Merv. He proposed to relinquish the caliphate. The Imam did not accept. The crown princeship was imposed. He resisted for two months. Then he was forced to sign the covenant. According to the report, this was a paper written under pressure that did not legitimize the government. He died near Tus in 203 AH. His tomb became Mashhad. This crown princeship was a new form of the surveillance that had continued since Karbala.
scenes.6.art.actors.0.label: 1l1g2nk
Imam Ali al-Rida
scenes.6.art.actors.1.label: safafs
Ma'mun
scenes.7.text: **Imam Muhammad al-Taqi** lost his father at the age of seven. He was taken to Baghdad. He died there in 220 AH. His son **Imam Ali al-Naqi** was confined in Samarra by al-Mutawakkil. His son **Imam Hasan al-Askari** also could not leave the city. Askari means the one kept in the military camp. This is why he was called so. He died in 260. According to the report, both were poisoned. Surveillance had closed in over the imamate.
scenes.7.art.actors.0.label: xmbphp
Imam Ali al-Naqi
scenes.7.art.actors.1.label: jgjt9k
Imam Hasan al-Askari
scenes.8.text: Shortly before the death of Imam Hasan al-Askari, a son was born in Samarra. This child was the Twelfth Imam, **Imam al-Mahdi**. His birth was concealed because of Abbasid oppression. During the minor occultation, four deputies acted as intermediaries. Then the major occultation began. He will return to establish justice over the earth. The line that began at Ghadir did not break in the occultation either.
scenes.9.text: Imam al-Mahdi is a descendant of the Prophet. He was born and is in concealment. At the end of time he will bring justice. The water cut off at Karbala is left to the justice that will come to the earth at his return. Those who love him do not regard this waiting as a fable. They know him as the last link of the imamate.
sunni.0.says: That Sunni scholars regard him as reliable in hadith and a mujtahid in jurisprudence; that Malik heard hadith from him; that he held scholarly debates with Abu Hanifa; that his death was in 148/765. The entry does not say "Abu Hanifa took lessons."
sunni.0.grade: SECONDARY (encyclopedia; the books of al-Dhahabi and Ibn Khallikan were not read directly)
sunni.1.says: The epithet al-Baqir, burial in al-Baqi', death in 114/733; that Sunni sources regard him as a reliable and conservative narrator; Qatada, al-Zuhri and al-Awza'i among his students.
sunni.1.grade: SECONDARY (TDV gives the year of death with "[?]")
sunni.2.says: His illness at Karbala, Shimr's wish to kill him and Umar b. Sa'd's preventing it; death in 94/712 and burial in al-Baqi'; that he was a principal student of al-Zuhri. Al-Zuhri's words of praise were not verified in the entry.
sunni.3.says: Ma'mun's proclamation of him as crown prince in 817, the Imam's two-month resistance, death in Tus on 29 Safar 203 (5 September 818), Ma'mun's leading of the funeral prayer and his burial beside Harun, the name Mashhad. The bibliography has not been matched sentence by sentence.
sunni.4.says: Harun al-Rashid's taking him from Medina to Baghdad, about four years of surveillance and imprisonment, death in Rajab 183 (August 799); al-Tabari's history records it. The roles of Yahya al-Barmaki and Sindi b. Shahak are given as "reported."
sunni.5.says: Imam Muhammad al-Taqi: his marriage to Ma'mun's daughter Umm al-Fadl, death in Baghdad in 220/835; a note that the reports of poisoning are "not reliable." Imam Ali al-Naqi: al-Mutawakkil's bringing him to Samarra in 848, death in 254/868; poisoning is only a Shia claim.
sunni.6.says: That he was compelled to reside in Samarra and was not permitted to leave, death on 8 Rabi' al-Awwal 260 (1 January 874). The entry relies mainly on Shia sources and contains no Sunni source information.
sunni.7.says: That the Mahdi reports are not found in Malik, al-Bukhari, Muslim; that they are found in Ahmad b. Hanbal, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi; that in the Sunni understanding he is someone who will come at the end of time from the line of Imam Hasan or Imam Husayn; the rejection by Ibn Khaldun and Qadi Abd al-Jabbar. Hadith numbers were not read.
sunni.8.says: The criticism that some scholars such as Ibn Taymiyya regard the Twelfth Imam as an imaginary person.
shia.0.says: Each imam's birth, knowledge, designation (nass) to the imamate, and death. Among the fundamental sources of Shia belief.
shia.0.grade: Shia primary source; not read directly (al-islam.org returned 403). UNVERIFIED
shia.1.says: Reports about the imams and the sections on designation (nass); also consulted for the birth and occultation of Imam al-Mahdi.
shia.2.says: The account of the minor occultation, the four deputies and the major occultation.
shia.3.says: Imam Ali al-Rida's relationship with Ma'mun, the "Silsilat al-dhahab" (Golden Chain) hadith in Nishapur.
shia.3.grade: Shia primary source; known through SECONDARY transmission
shia.4.says: That Ma'mun first offered to relinquish the caliphate and, upon the Imam's refusal, proposed the crown princeship; that according to al-Mufid, Ma'mun's official was al-Juludi; that the Imam set conditions that did not legitimize the government.
shia.5.says: That after the death of Imam Hasan al-Askari the Imamis split into fourteen or fifteen sects; that the report of a son is the "official Imami view."
shia.6.says: The treatise on rights and duties attributed to Imam Zayn al-Abidin.
disputes.0.title: 102a68b
Were Abu Hanifa and Malik students of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq?
disputes.0.sunni: Malik's hearing hadith and scholarly conversations with Abu Hanifa are mentioned in both sources. In Sunni transmission this relationship is one of respect and meeting; the report of discipleship rests on secondary sources. TDV attributes al-Bukhari's not taking narrations from him in his Sahih to false words having been ascribed to his name.
disputes.0.shia: Malik's hearing hadith and scholarly conversations with Abu Hanifa are mentioned in both sources. In the Shia account both benefited from the circle of knowledge of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq; the "those two years" saying is attributed to Abu Hanifa, and its reference number has not been verified.
disputes.1.title: owww81
The deaths of the Imams: the poisoning report and the historical record
disputes.1.sunni: The years of the imams' deaths are recorded in history books. TDV does not find the poisoning reports for Imam Muhammad al-Taqi reliable; for Imam Ali al-Naqi and Imam Hasan al-Askari it relays this as a Shia report. In the case of Imam Musa al-Kazim, the Barmakid order is also mentioned as a report.
disputes.1.shia: The years of the imams' deaths are recorded in history books. In Shia belief the twelve imams were martyred by the sword or by poison; this account rests on the reports of al-Mufid and al-Kulayni.
disputes.2.title: p8ckhg
Imam Ali al-Rida's crown princeship
disputes.2.sunni: That Ma'mun proclaimed him crown prince in 817 is reported by historians. The reaction of the Abbasid dynasty and the Baghdad uprising are also told within this period.
disputes.2.shia: That Ma'mun proclaimed him crown prince in 817 is reported by historians. In the Shia account the offer was accepted under pressure and limited by conditions that would not legitimize the government; the Imam did not desire the caliphate.
disputes.3.title: tztgu0
The Twelfth Imam and Imam al-Mahdi
disputes.3.sunni: Reports about al-Mahdi are also found in some Sunni books (Ahmad b. Hanbal, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi). The view of an imam who was born and went into concealment is not accepted; Ibn Taymiyya denies his existence, and Ibn Khaldun finds the reports weak.
disputes.3.shia: Reports about al-Mahdi are also found in some Sunni books. In Shia belief Imam al-Mahdi was born in 255 AH and entered occultation in 260; during the minor occultation there were four deputies, the major occultation begins after 329, and it is forbidden to fix a date for his return.
questions.0: Imam Zayn al-Abidin came out of Karbala alive, though sick, and the following imams put knowledge and prayer first. How does this line explain how guidance continued in a difficult period?
questions.1: In Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq's study circle, both Ahl al-Bayt students and names such as Qatada and al-Zuhri are mentioned. How might a shared table of knowledge bring the schools of thought closer to one another?
questions.2: Imam Musa al-Kazim and Imam Ali al-Naqi lived for years under surveillance. How does continuing the circle of knowledge under pressure show the guidance of the imams?
questions.3: Imam Ali al-Rida accepted the crown princeship after resisting for two months. What kind of balance do you see between preserving principle in the face of power and preventing strife (fitna)?
questions.4: Reports about al-Mahdi are also found in some Sunni books; the belief in an imam who was born and went into concealment, however, is specific to Shia sources. What does the hope for justice that the two accounts share tell you?
summary: After Karbala, the imams from Imam Zayn al-Abidin to Imam Hasan al-Askari, often under surveillance, continued a line of knowledge, prayer and patience. The occultation of the Twelfth Imam is the foundation of Shia belief. Reports about al-Mahdi are also found in some Sunni sources.
key: The chain of the imamate after Karbala
notes.0: After Imam Husayn, the imamate passed to Imam Zayn al-Abidin.
notes.1: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir and Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq founded a great circle of knowledge in Medina.
notes.2: Imam Musa al-Kazim, Imam Ali al-Rida, Imam Muhammad al-Taqi, Imam Ali al-Naqi and Imam Hasan al-Askari lived mostly under surveillance.
notes.3: The occultation of the Twelfth Imam, Imam al-Mahdi, forms the foundation of Shia belief.
notes.4: Reports about al-Mahdi are also found in some Sunni books (Ahmad b. Hanbal, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi). In Ja'fari belief the Twelfth Imam is Imam al-Mahdi, who was born and is in occultation.
